arxiv-2108-10024.title: Tagging the initial-state gluon Journal: Eur. Phys. J. C
arxiv-2108-10024.creator: Simone Caletti e1,addr1, Oleh Fedkevych e2,addr1, Simone Marzani e3,addr1, Daniel Reichelt e4,addr2
arxiv-2108-10024.description: Abstract We study the production of an electroweak boson in association with jets, in processes where the jet with the highest transverse momentum is identified as quark-initiated. The quark/gluon tagging procedure is realised by a cut on a jet angularity and it is therefore theoretically well-defined and exhibits infrared and collinear safety.

arxiv-2203-13106.title: An overview of new measurements of flow, chirality, and vorticity from STAR experiment
arxiv-2203-13106.creator: Chunjian Zhang (for the STAR Collaboration)
arxiv-2203-13106.description: Abstract In relativistic heavy-ion collisions, the properties of quark-gluon plasma (QGP) and complex dynamics of multi-scale processes in Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD) are studied by analyzing the final state produced particles in a variety of different ways. In these proceedings, we present an overview of new detailed measurements of flow, chirality, and vorticity by the STAR experiment at RHIC.

arxiv-2209-00719.title: A spherically symmetric gravitational solution of nearly conformally flat metric measure space
arxiv-2209-00719.creator: S.Oghbaiee, N. Rahmanpour, H. Shojaie
arxiv-2209-00719.description: Abstract In this manuscript, we study the nearly flat approximation of a conformally invariant gravitational theory in metric measure space (MMS). In addition, we investigate the transformation of the energy-momentum tensor in this context and obtain the vacuum solution of MMS and its weak field limit in the spherically symmetric coordinates.

arxiv-2309-02253.title: MA-VAE: Multi-head Attention-based Variational Autoencoder Approach for Anomaly Detection in Multivariate Time-series Applied to Automotive Endurance Powertrain Testing
arxiv-2309-02253.creator: Lucas Correia 1 2 , Jan-Christoph Goos 1 , Philipp Klein 1 , Thomas Bäck 2 and Anna V. Kononova 2 1 Mercedes-Benz AG, Stuttgart, Germany 2 Leiden University, Leiden, The Netherlands lucas.correia@mercedes-benz.com
arxiv-2309-02253.description: Abstract A clear need for automatic anomaly detection applied to automotive testing has emerged as more and more attention is paid to the data recorded and manual evaluation by humans reaches its capacity. Such real-world data is massive, diverse, multivariate and temporal in nature, therefore requiring modelling of the testee behaviour.

arxiv-2402-14593.title: Bayesian inference of thermal effects in dense matter within the covariant density functional theory
arxiv-2402-14593.creator: Adriana R. Raduta, Mikhail V. Beznogov, Micaela Oertel
arxiv-2402-14593.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Adriana R. Raduta, Mikhail V. Beznogov, Micaela Oertel. The high temperatures reached in a proto-neutron star or during the post-merger phase of a binary neutron star coalescence lead to non-negligible thermal effects on the equation of state (EOS) of dense nuclear matter (NM). Here we study these effects within the covariant density functional theory employing the posteriors of a Bayesian inference, which encompasses a large sample of EOS models. Different densities and temperatures are considered.

arxiv-2408-12760.title: Hierarchical Attention and Parallel Filter Fusion Network for Multi-Source Data Classification
arxiv-2408-12760.creator: Han Luo, Feng Gao, Junyu Dong, Lin Qi
arxiv-2408-12760.description: Abstract Hyperspectral image (HSI) and synthetic aperture radar (SAR) data joint classification is a crucial and yet challenging task in the field of remote sensing image interpretation. However, feature modeling in existing methods is deficient to exploit the abundant global, spectral, and local features simultaneously, leading to sub-optimal classification performance.

arxiv-2412-06683.title: A Decoupled Channel Estimation Method for Beyond Diagonal RIS
arxiv-2412-06683.creator: Bruno Sokal, Fazal-E-Asim, André L. F. de Almeida, Hongyu Li, and Bruno Clerckx
arxiv-2412-06683.description: Abstract Beyond diagonal reconfigurable intelligent surface (BD-RIS) is a new architecture for RIS where elements are interconnected to provide more wave manipulation flexibility than traditional single-connected RIS, enhancing data rate and coverage. However, channel estimation for BD-RIS is challenging due to the more complex multiple-connection structure involving their scattering elements.

arxiv-2510-11868.title: Improving Knowledge Graph Embeddings through Contrastive Learning with Negative Statements Conference: International Conference on Knowledge Capture; December 10–12, 2025; Ohio, USA
arxiv-2510-11868.creator: Rita T. Sousa, Heiko Paulheim
arxiv-2510-11868.description: Abstract . Knowledge graphs represent information as structured triples and serve as the backbone for a wide range of applications, including question answering, link prediction, and recommendation systems. A prominent line of research for exploring knowledge graphs involves graph embedding methods, where entities and relations are represented in low-dimensional vector spaces that capture underlying semantics and structure.

pmc-12374990.title: RNN-Bi-LSTM spectrum sensing algorithm for NOMA waveform with diverse channel conditions
pmc-12374990.creator: Arun Kumar, Aziz Nanthaamornphong, Mehedi Masud
pmc-12374990.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access (NOMA) has emerged as a prominent technique for enhancing spectral efficiency in beyond-fifth-generation (5G) and sixth-generation (6G) wireless systems. However, its performance is highly dependent on channel conditions, necessitating robust spectrum-sensing methods. This study proposes a novel Recurrent Neural Network (RNN)-based Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (RNN-Bi-LSTM) model to enhance the spectral performance of NOMA under various channel conditions, particularly the Rician and Rayleigh fading channels.

pmc-12449292.title: Advancing our understanding of the influence of myeloid-derived suppressor cells in chronic myeloid leukemia
pmc-12449292.creator: Xing Meng, Yue Zhang, Hong Xu, Yanyan Zhang, Hao He, Jianmin Ma, Xiaoyan Zhang
pmc-12449292.description: Chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) is a malignant clonal proliferative disease originating from hematopoietic stem cells. While treatment with tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) effectively eliminates the majority of leukemia cells in patients, residual leukemia cells can still be detected in those achieving deep molecular remission, ultimately leading to drug resistance or relapse. But the exact mechanism is unclear.

pmc-13002731.title: Personalized 3D surgical planning in liver transplantation: A new era in preoperative assessment and management of vascular and biliary complications
pmc-13002731.creator: Victor Lopez-Lopez, Cecilia Maina, Lucía Hernández-Ramos, Pedro Cascales-Campos, Alberto Baroja-Mazo, Dilmurodjon Eshmuminov, Jose Antonio-Pons, Guillermo Carbonell, Sergio Hernández-Kakauridze, Miguel Rodriguez-Velázquez, Francisco Sánchez-Bueno, Ricardo Robles-Campos, Miguel A Gómez-Bravo, Pablo R
pmc-13002731.description: PurposeThis study aimed to analyze next-generation 3D modeling software utility for personalized surgery in the field of liver transplantation.MethodsA retrospective cross-sectional pilot study was conducted at two referral centers including cases of liver transplantation-related complications – either preoperative portal vein thrombosis (PVT) or postoperative portal, arterial or biliary strictures – for which high-quality radiologic imaging was available.

pmc-13253410.title: An inflammatory–nutritional machine learning model for risk stratification of hospital-acquired pneumonia in traumatic brain injury: a multicenter study
pmc-13253410.creator: Chenzhu Cai, Zhenyu Fan, Longjie Chen, Shanglu Lin, Mingfa Cai, Zhen Qi, Xieli Guo
pmc-13253410.description: BackgroundHospital-acquired pneumonia (HAP) is a frequent and serious complication following traumatic brain injury (TBI), leading to prolonged hospitalization and poor functional outcomes. Early identification of patients at high risk of HAP remains challenging. Systemic inflammation and nutritional status are recognized contributors to post-TBI infection susceptibility; however, these factors are not adequately incorporated into existing predictive models.

pmc-13256901.creator: Yugal Goel, Mya A. Arellano, Kendall O’Daniel, Donovan A. Argueta, Reina Lomeli, Naomi Lomeli, Dahlia A. Ordaz, Daniela A. Bota, Vidhya Kumaresan, Kalpna Gupta
pmc-13256901.description: Primary neuronal cultures from the brain are critical for investigating disease-specific cellular and molecular mechanisms in mouse models. Current methods for obtaining primary cultures require embryonic brains that are affected by embryonic lethality and genotypic characterization in severe disease models such as sickle cell disease (SCD).
